title: Compliance and Auditing
description: Understand Linux audit frameworks, log integrity, and how to satisfy compliance requirements without slowing delivery.

data.text: Compliance and auditing sound like bureaucracy, but they are really about trust: can you prove who did what, and can you prove your systems stayed secure? Linux provides native auditing tools that answer both questions without slowing developers down.
This lesson explains the Linux audit subsystem, how to protect log integrity, and how to align operational practices with common compliance frameworks.
The Linux Audit system records security events such as file access, user logins, and system calls. It is enabled through `auditd`, which writes immutable logs that even root cannot easily alter.

data.title: Installing and starting auditd
data.code:
# Install auditd (Debian/Ubuntu)
sudo apt-get install auditd audispd-plugins

# Start and enable the service
sudo systemctl enable --now auditd

# Check audit daemon status
sudo systemctl status auditd

data.title: Watching a sensitive file for changes
data.code:
# Monitor /etc/ssh/sshd_config for all writes
sudo auditctl -w /etc/ssh/sshd_config -p wa -k sshd-config-change

# List current audit rules
sudo auditctl -l

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Tag audit rules with a key such as sshd-config-change so you can filter later. Without keys, audit logs become impossible to search when you need them most.
Audit logs are only useful if they are trustworthy. Protect them from tampering by writing to a remote syslog server, enabling immutable logs, and verifying checksums regularly.

items: Forward logs to a remote syslog server immediately
Set immutable append-only attributes on log files
Hash logs with sha256sum and compare against baselines
Restrict access to log directories with chmod 750

data.text: You do not need to memorize every regulation. Most frameworks share the same core controls: access logging, change management, encryption, and incident response. Map your Linux controls to these pillars.

items: Enable auditd on all production servers
Define audit rules for critical files and binaries
Forward logs to a remote, immutable store
Map Linux controls to your compliance framework quarterly
Document exceptions and obtain written approval

data.title: Summary
data.text: Compliance is about evidence, not paperwork. Use Linux audit tools to capture tamper-resistant logs, protect log integrity with remote forwarding, and align your controls with recognized frameworks. Good auditing prevents blame-shifting and speeds up investigations.
